=== CONSENSUS FINDINGS ===
- .github/workflows/plan.yml:321 | severity=high | confidence=4
  flagged_by: [minimax_minimax-m3]
  PROBLEM: The grep `outcome=refused reason=pr_not_open$` is claimed never to match because the resolver stderr line is claimed to end with `pr=<N> run=<id>`, so `not_open_pr` would always be empty.
  WHY: An empty `PLAN_PR_NOT_OPEN_PR` would make the marker carry `pr=` instead of the real PR number. Severity is MAJOR here, and anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5 and z-ai_glm-5_3-flash refuted the claim, so the reviewers disagree on whether it is valid.
- .github/workflows/plan.yml:985-994 | severity=low | confidence=3
  flagged_by: [anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5, minimax_minimax-m3]
  PROBLEM: The `pr_not_open_unresolved` body uses `#${pr:-unknown}` in the prose but bare `pr=${pr}` in the marker, so an empty PR number renders differently in the two places.
  WHY: A downstream parser keyed on `pr=<digits>` could drop the hand-off if the PR number is empty. anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5 rated it NIT with confidence 2 and said it cannot occur in practice. minimax_minimax-m3 rated it NIT with confidence 3.
- tests/test_plan_superseded_merged_pr_workflow.py:447-454 | severity=low | confidence=3
  flagged_by: [minimax_minimax-m3, z-ai_glm-5_3-flash]
  PROBLEM: No test covers the hand-off path where the label edit succeeds and the comment POST fails (`comment_state=failed`).
  WHY: A regression in the POST branch could leave the issue at `ai:blocked` with no `ai:plan-pr-not-open:v1` marker, and no test would catch it. anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5 also raised this gap and judged it a test-coverage nit.
=== END CONSENSUS FINDINGS ===

=== FINDINGS FROM anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5 ===
- .github/workflows/plan.yml:(`pr_not_open_unresolved` body construction) | severity=low | confidence=2
  PROBLEM: If both the resolver output and the classifier PR number are empty, the prose reads "pull request #unknown" while the marker reads `pr=`.
  WHY: The PR number is always present on the `pr_not_open` path, so the mismatch only matters if the resolver's output format changes.
- (Correctness) The reviewer refuted minimax's finding on plan.yml:321 and reported no correctness findings. (Also noted as a test-coverage nit: a comment POST failure after a successful label edit is untested. It reported no severity or confidence for this note.)
=== END FINDINGS FROM anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5 ===

=== FINDINGS FROM minimax_minimax-m3 ===
- .github/workflows/plan.yml:321 | severity=high | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: The grep `$` anchor requires the resolver stderr line to end with `pr_not_open`, but the line is claimed to end with `pr=<N> run=<id>`, so `not_open_pr` would always be empty.
  WHY: The marker would carry an empty `pr=`. The reviewer says the contract test `tests/test_workflow_checkout_integration_ref_audit.py:430` does not exercise the real format.
- .github/workflows/plan.yml:321 | severity=high | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: Suggested fix: drop the `$` anchor, or replace it with `[[:space:]]` or `\s`, and update the contract test fixture to write a stderr line that ends with `pr=...` and `run=...`.
  WHY: Without this, the resolver's PR number is lost whenever `pr_not_open` is the failure reason and the classifier has not pre-populated `pr_number`.
- .github/workflows/plan.yml:985-994 | severity=low | confidence=3
  PROBLEM: The body uses `${pr:-unknown}` in the prose but bare `${pr}` in the `ai:plan-pr-not-open:v1` marker.
  WHY: A downstream parser keyed on `pr=<digits>` would silently drop the hand-off if the PR number is empty.
- tests/test_plan_superseded_merged_pr_workflow.py:443-454 | severity=low | confidence=3
  PROBLEM: There is no test for `label_state=applied` followed by a failed `gh api ... /comments` POST.
  WHY: A regression in the POST branch would leave a half-hand-off with no marker comment, and no test would catch it.
=== END FINDINGS FROM minimax_minimax-m3 ===

  WHY: A regression that swallowed the POST failure, such as a `|| true` added to line 994, would leave the issue at `ai:blocked` with no marker, and no test would catch it.
